title: Fonio Pilaf with Dates, Carrots and Peanuts
author: Pierre Thiam
desc: Medjool dates, roasted peanuts, cayenne and carrots softened in red palm oil, fonio stirred in with stock, then baked covered in a square dish — Thiam’s Thanksgiving stuffing.
longDesc: Thiam serves this at his Thanksgiving table because he finds it lighter than a bread stuffing. Palm oil warms in a saucepan; dates, half the peanuts, cayenne and diced carrots cook 8 to 10 minutes until the carrots soften slightly. Fonio is stirred into the oil, stock goes in, and the pot is covered and cooked without stirring about three minutes until the grains absorb the stock. It is then transferred to a greased 8-inch square dish, covered with foil, and baked about 20 minutes at 325° until tender and heated through, fluffed, seasoned and topped with the remaining peanuts and parsley.
ingredients: 1/4 cup red palm oil or vegetable oil, plus more for greasing
5 oz pitted Medjool dates, roughly chopped
1/2 cup roughly chopped unsalted roasted peanuts, divided
1 cup fonio or quinoa, rinsed and drained
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper — quantities not printed
steps: Heat the oven to 325° (the page prints no unit). In a medium saucepan over medium heat, warm the palm oil. Add the dates, 1/4 cup of the peanuts, the cayenne and the carrots and cook, stirring, 8 to 10 minutes, until the carrots soften slightly.
Add the fonio and stir to coat in the oil. Add the stock and bring to a boil. Cover and cook without stirring about 3 minutes, until the fonio absorbs all the stock.
Transfer to the baking dish greased with palm oil and smooth the top. Cover with foil and bake about 20 minutes, until tender and heated through.
Uncover, fluff with a fork and season with salt and pepper. Move to a serving bowl and top with the remaining peanuts and the parsley.
chefTips: Do not stir while the fonio absorbs the stock — about three minutes covered.
Grease the dish with palm oil, as the page says.
Couscous or quinoa can replace the fonio in equal amounts.
The only oven temperature in the fonio set is 325°, with no unit printed.
commonMistakes: Baking uncovered and drying it out.
reheating: Covered in a 325° oven or a splash of stock on the stove.
healthBenefits: Dates and carrots add fibre and potassium.
Peanuts add protein and healthy fats.
culturalNote: The parent article, ‘A Brooklyn Thanksgiving with the Flavors of Senegal’, is where this appeared. The headnote calls fonio ‘a delightfully nutty-tasting type of millet’ and ‘a ubiquitous staple in Senegal’.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Fonio Pilaf With Dates, Carrots, and Peanuts’. Byline: ‘By Pierre Thiam’. Saveur, originally 16 November 2015, updated 28 March 2021. Yield: ‘serves 6-8’ (7 used here). Time: 45 minutes. TWO-PASS on every quantity, with the original fraction-slash characters preserved on both passes. The page also prints ‘1⁄4 cup’ and ‘1/4-inch’ with different slashes.

Cues in short fragments: ‘until the carrots soften slightly’; ‘until the fonio absorbs all the stock’; ‘until tender and warmed through’. The oven temperature, ‘325°’, has no unit; pass one rendered it ‘325°F’.
A reprint exists at yolele.com under the byline ‘Yolele’; not separately fetched.
